new_need.sentence: How many people actually read LindyBooks these days?

questions.question: How many distinct real people actually read LindyBooks in the recent past (last 30 days)?
questions.quantity: Distinct humans who engaged with LindyBooks content (loaded and read/engaged, not merely visited or bounced; e.g. meaningful time on content, scroll depth, or reading/opening a book or issue) in the window
questions.population: Distinct human readers/users of LindyBooks who actually consumed content
exclude: bounces and drive-by visits with no real reading
duplicate counts of the same person across devices where detectable
subscribers or account holders who did not read in the window

questions.question: Is the number of actual readers growing, flat, or shrinking compared with the prior period?
questions.quantity: Change in distinct actual readers, 30d vs previous 30d

capabilities.built_for: I want to know, at a glance, how many real people are actually using LindyBooks.
questions: How many distinct real human people actively used LindyBooks in the recent period?
For context, how many real registered accounts exist versus those actively used?
metrics: How many distinct real human people actively used LindyBooks in the r…
Number of paid donations/payments to the fund

relation.description: same_need: built to answer what the new need asks (however well it answers today); can_do: the new request is something it can already do through its interface, as it is; extend: it holds the data or is the place the principal uses for this, but lacks something the request needs; unrelated

covered.description: ids of the new questions or requirements it covers

gaps.description: what the new need asks that it cannot do today

gaps: Not confirmed that it defines 'active' as actual reading/engagement (time on content, scroll depth) rather than just usage/logins
Not confirmed it excludes bots, staff traffic and bounces, or de-duplicates people across devices
No stated prior-period comparison (30d vs previous 30d) or percent change/direction metric
Needs a trend or growth verdict derived from distinct readers
